clinician.final_diagnosis: Acute hemorrhagic oedema of infancy (AHEI), also named Finkelstein disease, Seidlmayer disease, Finkelstein-Seidlmayer disease, rosette form purpura, infantile post-infectious iris-like purpura and medallion-like purpura—a cutaneous leukocytoclastic small-vessel vasculitis presenting with localized purpuric large skin plaques frequently associated with fever and oedema
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-month-old previously healthy girl presented with petechiae on the soft palate 24 hours after initial onset. She had a recent history of MMR vaccination 12 days prior and mild febrile diarrhea 8 days before presentation. Initial evaluation showed normal platelet count (171,000/mm³), excluding ITP. Over the following 2 days, she developed fever (maximum 38.3°C) and progressive petechial-hemorrhagic rash with sharp margins affecting limbs, face, and auricles, accompanied by a strong edematous component. On admission, her general condition was good. Laboratory studies showed elevated CRP (3.58 mg/dL) without leukocytosis and normal platelet count (180,000/mm³). On the second day of hospitalization, bilateral edema of the metacarpophalangeal joints with joint pain developed, which responded to paracetamol and resolved within one week. Abdominal ultrasound excluded visceral involvement. The skin manifestations progressively diminished and disappeared spontaneously within 3 weeks, leaving no sequelae.
